reviews.comment: Spent most of class instead of further explaining the topics. If you have trouble paying attention in class, you will struggle
Awesome professor. Took his class over the summer and can say you can only fail if you don't pay attention well to the lecture contents.

He's such a sweet professor and constantly makes jokes. He moves super quickly through the work and assigns a lot of homework, so if you fall behind it starts to stack up. If you aren't following along then you will fall behind. Prepare yourself and attend MLC events (only saying because I suck at math) to stay on top of the lessons.
He is super sweet, but maybe not the best at explaining concepts thoroughly. The class doesn't have much review material to learn the concepts outside of lecture.

Dr. White is nice and understands his material, but the pace may be considered fast to some. Your outcome of this class all depends on your own study habits and how willing you are to learn the material.

Dr. White is a super sweet guy that knows how to teach very well. His lectures occasionally didn't make sense because he is very soft spoken in general. I had class in chem 100 and even with a mic you could barely hear him. Overall, he taught the course very well and is super understanding. Take the practice exams and you'll do fine on exams.

Great guy, lectures are very clear and he explained things quite well. I can understand how his lectures may be a bit difficult to understand for someone who isn't used to upper-level math terminology and proof-based mathematics. But if you put in the work, no reason this class isn't an easy A.

I really enjoyed Professor White's class. I'd say White's teaching was mediocre. I felt there were times he'd go off on tangents and no one knew what he was saying. Exams were fair. Just study the material well. Don't memorize. If you don't like proofs, I wouldn't recommend him because he's very proof-heavy in my opinion. I found 308 easier.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While the material is very confusing and this professor can go very fast in lectures I still enjoyed the class. He posted all his notes in canvas so attendance is not mandatory with the exception of quizzes that were usually weekly. Exams were easy and fair.

Dr. White is a decent professor, but you might get lost in theory during lectures. Make sure you pay attention to when he goes over examples as that is where the majority of the learning will be. His exam reviews are very helpful for exams and he's a solid pick for linear algebra.

I found that Dr. White was a solid professor, with no major complaints. The lectures and homeworks were enough for me to do great in this class, although the textbook did help to check my understanding sometimes. There is also sometimes extra credit in this class, and the grading is pretty lax.

He was a good professor that cares about his students. He made sure to know all of the students taking the courses names. While he does grade hard, if you go to class and pay attention you should do fine. The 2 essays are def grade boosters, but the exams aren't too difficult. Homework does take a long time, though.

Prof White is a very nice and funny dude who cares about his students. The grading was pretty chill overall. The class was not very hard but sometimes it would get very confusing and abstract. Nothing you cant try and teach yourself the day before an exam. As long as you put in effort you will be fine.

Math 140 is already a tough subject because it bounces around and doesn't build on itself. White isn't great at teaching the subject, but he is really nice and funny. I recommend going to help sessions and his office hours. He has pop quizzes and iClickers frequently, so going to class will help your grade. He wasn't the worst, but not the best.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: It's math so it really depends on you more than the prof. He's not the worst but not the best. His lectures were fine but you kinda need to know the content beforehand to follow along with him. If you've taken algebra 2 or calc in high school you should be fine. he does pop quizzes randomly so go to class. not great at responding to emails.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Math 140 had been my Achilles' heel at A&M, and this was my 3rd attempt at passing the class. I firmly believe that of the 3 professors I had, Dr. White was the most fair, and the best teacher of the subject. I was honestly really nervous when I had initially saw his ratings, but found them to be rather deceiving. Dr. White is an AWSOME guy!

Professor White is a very good professor. I took AP AB Calculus in high school, so it was a lot easier for me, but he did a good job lecturing. He has all of his notes on canvas. He could be a little confusing at times, and his work was a little scattered. Good guy, does have pop quizzes but they are group. Would take again, but pay attention.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof White was very chill and nice and I respected him a lot. BUT, I pretty much had to teach myself this entire course because he would get often confused and mess up problems so it was really hard to actually learn. If you already know calculus, you prob will be fine. If not, get ready to move into the Math Learning Center for the next 4 months.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor White is good and definitely gets you all the information you need. All math140 classes have the same amount of work so it doesn't really make a difference what professor you have. However, do beware of quizzes, he doesn't usually say which day we're having them so I would try not to skip class.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. White is definitely very smart, but he does not really explain what he is doing half the time. If you aren't good at math or have not taken calculus before, it is a bit of a struggle. If you do and understand the reviews he posts for the tests, you can definitely pass.

If you didn't take calculus in high school, don't take this course with Dr. White. He IS a good professor, but not if you don't already have an understanding of what he's teaching. Since I didn't take calculus in high school, this class was very difficult for me and his lectures don't really help me learn the material.

Shocked at how low Dr White's ratings are. Like yes, it's a math class, you're not gonna be waking up jumping for joy to go to his lectures. It is what it is. However, Dr White is super laid back and goes in there, does the notes, and heads out. I respect that in a professor. If you have a basic concept of college algebra, you're golden.

Dr. White was alright, as his lectures could be hard to follow, and his OneNote with the notes could become really confusing since he tends to skip over things, and also make mistakes in his math. Tests weren't hard since they were really similar to his reviews, so for the most part, a pretty straightforward class that requires a decent bit of work

Your grade will be determined by 1 homework/week plus 3 exams.  Notes are posted online but can be difficult to follow. I didn't really attend lectures, but you can succeed in this class by studying the textbook and solving the practice problems in it.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My biggest issue with this class, keeping me from a 4 or 5 rating, was lectures were super difficult for me to follow. Notes were posted but were just written on a blank OneNote (no guided notes or slides) and I was often very confused and got lost in proofs. Saving grace of this class is that exam reviews were super helpful to prepare for exams.

Dr White made this the first fun math class for me. He is the most fair professor I have ever had. Old ratings are likely for the same professor, but they are outdated and inaccurate.

Lectures were often hard to follow since he's a big theory guy. But exams were like reviews and he's very generous with partial credit. Highly recommend taking him!

I honestly can't believe how low this guy's rating is. Maybe MATH 304 is different, but I really enjoyed taking this class. His lectures were good enough and followed the textbook. He always posted his notes on OneNote. Exams and homework were designed and graded very fairly. What's not to like?
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He's OK as a professor, definitely not the worst. He is a very, sweet man but the lectures were a bit hard to follow. He moves pretty quickly but if you need further clarification on something- he'll help you. In my opinion, if you take time to study outside of class you'll be fine. I winged it which is what resulted in me getting a C.

Very poor lecturer but also the exams were exactly like the reviews and the final got curved (no one, pre curve, passed the final). I ended up with an A very easily despite feeling lost the entire time. If you want a good understanding of 304, go elsewhere. If you want an easy A, take him.

Good guy, pretty funny too, overall I wouldn't say he's the worst math professor ever, but he definitely isn't the best, frankly he was middle of the road. The only reason I'm putting him low is because he didn't feel accessible outside of class because his office hours were incredibly confusing.

He made this course way harder to learn than it should've been. He is not good at explaining anything or answering questions. I learned more outside of his class than I ever did in class. Attendance isn't "required", but he does do pop quizzes often. His tests were more difficult than other professors, and his grading didn't always make sense.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Takes his time with during lectures to properly explain his notes. He also did his best the make himself available for students.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was really not that bad. His lectures were a bit boring but I don't think anyone can make math seem exiting. he shares his notes with the class and posts blank notes to follow along to. He seemed to like teaching and he tried to have fun with it. He made a lot of tiny jokes that took a second to understand and didn't always land.

Lectures mirrored the textbook, optional attendance. Great professor, humorous and accessible for questions. Easy mandatory HW. Helpful exam reviews, but no review for final (which was much more difficult.) My only critique was that he made many silly mistakes during lectures but owned up to it with bonus points on the final. I enjoyed the class!

He is a decent professor but moves through the lectures very fast. Even if you go to the lectures, you probably will need to watch the lecture videos online. There are around 2-3 homework assignments every week, an iClicker once a week, and group work once a week. Overall he is okay, but you will need to do some work outside of class to succeed.

His lectures move very fast and are hard to follow. The material itself is not too challenging when self taught. He solves problems without explaining anything. Overall a nice guy but I would not take his class again. Tests were unlike homework problems.
He's very smart but teaches kind of confusingly. A LOT of weekly homework which is much harder than the lecture practice questions.

Though he is very knowledgeable, he goes extremely fast in lectures, solves the problems confusingly, and often goes on irrelevant tangents when explaining a problem, which can be confusing. I would say it's mostly self-taught, but if you actually try on the homework, without using Photo Math, it can really help you learn. YouTube is clutch, too.

This is the worst professor I've ever had. Please do not take him if you want to learn & succeed. His notes are scribbles in which he writes in bright colors. He goes over problems that are that won't be on the exam and makes stupid jokes. Be prepared to teach yourself. I made an A in the class by teaching myself & looking at other prof's notes.

Do not get him!!! He made the final 100% free response and decided to count the whole problem wrong the second you make one mistake. Not to mention, when he posted the solutions to his practice final, they contained countless errors and mistakes. His lectures are hard to follow and many people do not attend.

He gets off topic and goes on rabbit trails. I spent more time correcting him than learning and stopped going all together and went to a different professor. He gives really difficult quizzes compared to other professors. He isn't horrid but I wouldn't recommend it if you have another choice, Aurispa is AMAZING!

Dr. White is not the best professor because he is not thorough in his explanations of problems. Out of the approximately 100 people in his lecture, only 20 attend because it is not very helpful. If he stayed on topic and worked through every problem (including all steps) he would be much better. Go to office hours for help. Really good 1on1.

This is the worst professor I have had in my entire academic career. His lectures are pointless to attend as he goes over "real world" problems that are never on the test. When he does try to cover the material in the curriculum, he does not finish solving the problem nor explain how to do it. His notes are chicken scratch and incomprehensible. NO!

I wish I could give him zeros. If you get stuck with this guy as your prof, bless your heart. Don't even bother going to lecture because it's not worth your time. His notes are disorganized and messy. He comes to class unprepared and makes crude and inappropriate jokes to seem "cool". Just don't sign up for his class. Seriously. Don't.

A typical lecture from Jacob White consists of a vaguely scribbled new concept, 2 even more vague examples,  answering of an off-topic question for 10 minutes, taking another 10 minutes to look up things related to it, cracking a junior-high level joke and laughing hysterically for the next 3 problems, then finally releasing class 20 minutes early.

-homework is due on a different daytime every week -lectures end 20 minutes early nearly every time, which sounds good but means he can't even teach the entire period -final is all open-ended questions -he gets distracted in lectures and looks up pointless things completely unrelated to math (Star Wars, the Golden Gate Bridge, etc)

I am not exaggerating when I say the Jacob White is the worst professor I have had during my time at Texas A&M. His Webassign HW has inconsistent due dates ranging  from 3pm to midnight on any day of the week, he is extremely unprepared and unequipped to teach in his lectures, and his final was all free response questions. Do NOT take Jacob White

I stopped regularly attending his class after the first exam. I really didn't learn anything in his lectures and depended on other professor's online notes. Examples done during class often had answers that couldn't be solved by hand. He depends a lot on Wolfram Alpha which gets annoying because you can't use it on exams (obviously).
